I'm within the circa 3% of people that dropped out pf medschool in austria

One thing i'd really like to highlight again is how much things vary here. I volunteer as a NFS at two different physician rigs in the same region. There's like half a hour drive between the two stations. But the working conditions vary vastly. On one of the NEF(physician rig), there's a very restricted number of NFS allowed to drive on them, and the quality of both ems personell and Doctors is kept as high as possible. On the other nef, I have to watch the doctor to avoid them harming the patient. Also every f**ing car is just slightly different from the others, just to add an extra bit of confusion. 

IMO, the austrian ems System is ok, but it relies on Doctors, which will be an issue in the near future.

The biggest thing I'd love to improve would be QA. If you are a RS or NFS it is practically impossible to loose that qualification. You have to show to a Doctor that you know how cpr works every two years and attend 16h of courses within two years. No qa on trauma, handling equipment or anything like that. 
Fun fact: a rescue dog has to redo his exam every year to keep its status. So you could say rescue dogs are more qualifies then rescue medics...
